guarantees.claim: For i=0..3, unused_prd_masking[i*WidthPRDRow +: WidthPRDRow] is continuously driven by the return value of function aes_prd_concat_bits(data_in_mask[i], unused_prd_msbs[i]).

assumptions.claim: Each data_in_mask[i] and unused_prd_msbs[i] must provide correct masking bits so that the resulting unused_prd_masking slice appropriately masks unused PRD data.
assumptions.cond: always, as this chunk continuously combines them
assumptions.risk: If inputs are not properly randomized or set to constant values (e.g., all zeros), the generated masking may be ineffective, exposing intermediate AES state to side-channel leakage.

uncertain_points.claim: The function aes_prd_concat_bits (not defined here) must correctly combine the two inputs into a WidthPRDRow-bit masking value; any flaw in its behavior could compromise the masking scheme.
uncertain_points.risk: If the function truncates, misaligns, or produces predictable outputs, unused bits may not be properly masked, leaking secret data.

uncertain_points.claim: The generate loop uses indices i=0..3, implying data_in_mask and unused_prd_msbs must have at least 4 elements; if these arrays are smaller, out-of-range reads will occur, potentially using uninitialized or constant values for masking.
uncertain_points.cond: when WidthPRDRow is parameterized and the arrays are not sized to match
uncertain_points.risk: Missing or invalid mask bits could result in unmasked PRD bits, breaking side-channel resistance.
